We rejoin our friend and semi-hero Roger Wilco as he rockets back toward his home planet, Xenon, which he hasn't seen since Space Quest II. Having successfully rescued those two ingrates from Andromeda, he decides a pit stop on Magmetheus is in order.
We have confirmation of his position, Master.
Off to Magmetheus with you then! It is time for Wilco to meet the fate which I have crafted for him.
During the descent to this cosmic canteen he is unaware of the interest that has been generated regarding his fate.
You go left to split 'em up! Mr. Wilco! Follow me and do exactly as I say! LET'S MOVE!
As our story begins, we find the Aluminum Mallard parked outside a seedy spaceport bar.
Are you Roger Wilco?
Please come with me.
Uh, yeah.
Hey, it's a gilled Thwarkian lambotraus! I havn't seen one of those in years!
We join Roger as he relates one of his greatly exaggerated tales of adventure. The aliens are only too happy to listen (as long as Roger is buying).
It looks like a cross between a praying mantis and Richard Nixon.
Must be a duck billed planetpuss.
Hello, Roger Wilco. Surprised to see an old friend? You have no idea how special this moment is for me. This is no chance encounter, I can assure you.
I have this one loose end to tie up before I begin my reign as The Supreme Being of All That Exists.

I DO NOT LIKE TO LOSE. You are a blemish on what would otherwise be a perfect record of domination, terror, and invincibility. Besides, I'm still a bit miffed about that asteroid deal in Space Quest II.
91	Anyway, to relieve the pain of my humiliation, and to prevent you from being a pain in my... future, YOU MUST DIE. My charges will take care of the messy details. It's been nice seeing you one last time. Men, do the dirty deed!"

So many unanswered questions. The future should prove most interesting for Roger - if he can stay out of trouble long enough to reach it. We're glad you could help Roger get through it all. Thank you for playing Space Quest IV.
A hazardous accumulation of unstructured structures blocks safe passage to the north.
The rubble is rough and jagged. No sense in risking injury this early in the adventure. We'll get to that later.
There's nothing like coating your lungs with rubble dust to get your adventure off to a great start.
It tastes okay, but you generally prefer your rubble Extra Chunky.
The old Bank of Xenon building held up fairly well. Too bad. They turned Roger down for a loan once.
Forget it! The doors and windows have been sealed with welded steel plating.
It smells like old money and new rust.
Okay, you get your last licks on the bank.
It looks like a surface suited for foot travel.
It tastes like all the other sidewalks you've ever tasted, weirdo.
It smells mostly of dust and dirt.
The rich aroma of hovercar exhaust fills your sinuses.
It tastes like you've just scraped your tongue to shreds on the pavement.

The clearing ends here. Jagged chunks of debris clog the north.
The rubble is rough and jagged. No sense in risking injury this early in the adventure. There's plenty of time for that later.
It smells like the remains of a flourishing civilization blasted to smithereens by an evil entity of immense power.
It doesn't taste half bad, considering what it smells like.
In the distance the skeletal remains of once proud structures jut weakly into the chemical-laden atmosphere.
If your tongue were that long... well, you can guess the rest.
The ruined buildings smell of death and destruction.
Creases from tank treads, craters from incoming ordnance, and gouges from fallen debris are the only deviations in an otherwise-smooth surface.
It has that unmistakeably tangy aroma of pressure-treated petrochemicals.
The taste of the street brings to mind all those wonderful times as a child that the local bully ground your face into the asphalt.
The large structure in the background captures your curiosity.
Nobody can reach that building from here with their tongue unless they're in a Leisure Suit Larry game.
It smells like trouble. What's going on in there?
There seems to be some light pouring through a row of three openings high up in the face of the distant structure.
You are at the northern boundary of a clearing in the midst of a battle-scarred city. An ominous-looking building is the only thing in sight which might contain life.
The rubble is rough and jagged. Your species wasn't designed to traverse this kind of terrain.
A featureless dirty white structure fills space to the east.
As is often the case in road design, many features were left out to make it a hazard-free experience.
